transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today? Is there something specific that’s been troubling you?

Um... well. I guess I'm here because of some trouble I've been having with my work. I was putting together a memorial piece for my aunt, and... I don't know. I just kept getting these awful, unwanted thoughts. 

Like... if I made one wrong choice with a color, or put a photo in the wrong place, it meant I was going to dishonor her somehow. Or that it proved I didn't love her enough. I tried to just ignore it, but... I couldn't brush them off like normal creative doubts. So... yeah. That's why I made the appointment.
Can you tell me more about these unwanted thoughts? Do they come up frequently, and do they cause you a lot of distress or take up a lot of your time?

Um... well, like I just mentioned, it was mostly while I was working on that memorial piece. They just... kept happening while I was trying to work. 

It was upsetting, yeah. Just... having those awful thoughts pop up that I was going to dishonor her. Usually, a wrong color choice or a bad photo placement is just an artistic mistake, but... this felt like it meant I didn't love her enough. I don't know. It took up time, I guess, mostly because I just couldn't brush them off like my normal doubts. I couldn't just move on from it.

When you had those upsetting thoughts, did you feel driven to do something over and over again—like checking, redoing parts of the memorial, or following certain rules—to ease the distress or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean... I would just keep rereading the text for the labels. Over and over. And... nudging the objects on the table, trying to get them exactly right. 

I'd check the layout photos a lot, too. Just... kept checking them until it finally felt, I don't know, settled. Even though I knew it was probably fine already. It just... ate up a lot of my studio time.
Outside of working on the memorial piece, have you noticed these thoughts or behaviors affecting other parts of your life, like your work, relationships, or daily activities?

Um... I guess it's mostly just my work. I'm still getting most of it done, but... I don't know. 

The extra time I lose in the studio... it did make me miss a grant deadline recently. And... I ended up backing out of a gallery talk. One I actually wanted to do. So... yeah. It's just affecting my work, mostly.
Do you feel like you have to follow specific routines or perform certain actions a particular way to keep things from going wrong, even if you know it might not make sense?

Um... well, like I said before... it's mostly just what I was doing with the memorial piece. 

I don't really have routines for everything, it's just... I guess I feel like I have to do those things I mentioned. The rereading the labels, and... moving the objects around until they're perfect. And checking the photos. I just... I have to keep doing it until that feeling goes away, until it feels settled. I know it doesn't really make sense, and it wastes my time, but... I just can't seem to stop until it feels right.
Can you describe how distressing these thoughts were when you were working on the memorial piece? Did they feel intrusive or unwanted?

Um... yeah, they were unwanted. It wasn't like... normal creative doubts, where you just wonder if a piece looks right. 

I just kept getting these awful thoughts that... that I was going to dishonor her somehow. Like if I made one wrong choice with a photo placement or... a color... it meant I didn't love her enough. I couldn't really just brush them off. So... yeah. It was pretty distressing, I guess.
Outside of working on the memorial piece, have you been feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling guilty or worthless?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, I was sad about my grandmother, obviously, but... I haven't really been feeling down like that. Or guilty. Just... frustrated with the art piece, I guess. That's all.
